newsitem.title: USA: Ivax, Bergen Brunswig deal off.
newsitem.headline: Ivax, Bergen Brunswig deal off.

text.p: Bergen Brunswig Corp. has called off its $1.6 billion takeover of IVAX Corp., which would have been the nation's first combination of a major drug wholesaler and a large maker of generic drugs.

In a statement issued late Thursday, Bergen Brunswig said it planned to file a lawsuit against IVAX alleging breach of their merger pact. In a separate statement, Ivax said Bergen terminated the merger without good cause.

Drug wholesaler Bergen, based in Orange, Calif., said in November that the two companies agreed to merge. In Thursday's statement, it said that while it was terminating its agreement with IVAX, it would continue to pursue a strategy aimed at managing supply channel costs.

"Notwithstanding the termination of the IVAX agreement, we will continue to pursue our strategy, recognising the valuable role that generics play," said Donald Roden, Bergen's president and chief executive officer.
A Bergen spokeswoman said she could not comment on precisely how the merger agreement had been breached because the matter was going into litigation.
"It involves things that have been occurring over the past few months," she said.
IVAX said it was prepared to proceed independently.

"Recognizing the possibility that the Bergen merger might not be approved or completed, we developed, together with our advisors, a number of contingency strategies geared toward the success of an independent IVAX, and look forward to announcing and implementing those strategies in the near term," IVAX Chairman Phillip Frost said.

An IVAX spokesman told Reuters the company could not comment or speculate about Bergen's allegations because it had not yet been served with the complaint. "We don't see any sound basis for their unilateral termination," he said.
The spokesman said IVAX had already fashioned contingency strategies, which it would announce shortly, but he declined to reveal the specifics of those strategies.
Ivax's stock closed Thursday at $12.375 on the American Stock Exchange, and Bergen ended at $31.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
